bull.b: Very low leverage reduces near-term balance-sheet pressure and leaves the company less exposed to interest obligations than a heavily indebted biotech. This provides greater financial flexibility while Tenaya advances clinical programs and seeks future funding or partnerships.

Moving away from a large internal manufacturing facility reduces long-term facility obligations while preserving process and assay expertise. An outsourced model can improve operational flexibility and allow resources to remain focused on clinical development and potential commercialization.

A multi-modality pipeline aimed at modifying or correcting underlying disease mechanisms gives Tenaya several potential approaches to important cardiovascular conditions. This focus may support differentiated clinical opportunities if programs demonstrate durable therapeutic benefit.

bear.b: The scale of ongoing losses shows that Tenaya remains far from sustainable profitability and must continue investing heavily before product revenues can support operations. Persistent negative earnings weaken internal funding capacity and increase dependence on future financing or partnerships.

Negative operating and free cash flow indicate that the business is consuming cash rather than funding development internally. Although annual operating burn improved from 2022 to 2025, the latest period does not show a steady path toward consistently lower burn.

The substantial decline in equity reflects the cumulative effect of ongoing losses and reduces the capital cushion supporting clinical development. A smaller equity base can constrain strategic flexibility and make future capital needs more consequential for existing shareholders.
